definitions.explanation: A state of physical exhaustion, loss of appetite, and general malaise caused by prolonged exposure to summer heat and humidity. A common condition in Japan's hot and humid summers. Composed of 夏 (summer) + バテる (to be worn out).

examples.japanese: {夏|なつ}バテで{食欲|しょくよく}がない。
examples.english: I have no appetite due to summer fatigue.

examples.japanese: {夏|なつ}バテしないように、しっかり{食|た}べよう。
examples.english: Let's eat well so we don't get summer fatigue.

examples.japanese: {毎年|まいとし}{八月|はちがつ}になると{夏|なつ}バテして、{何|なに}もやる{気|き}が{起|お}きなくなる。
examples.english: Every year when August comes, I get summer fatigue and lose all motivation.

notes:
USAGE:
Can function as a noun ({夏|なつ}バテ) or as a する verb ({夏|なつ}バテする). Symptoms include loss of appetite, fatigue, and difficulty sleeping. Very common topic in Japanese summer conversation.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {夏|なつ}バテする (to suffer from summer fatigue)
- {夏|なつ}バテ{防止|ぼうし} / {予防|よぼう} (preventing summer fatigue)
- {夏|なつ}バテ{対策|たいさく} (measures against summer fatigue)
- {夏|なつ}バテ{気味|ぎみ} (a touch of summer fatigue)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Japan's humid summers make {夏|なつ}バテ a widely shared experience. Traditional remedies include eating {鰻|うなぎ} (eel) on {土用|どよう}の{丑|うし}の{日|ひ} (midsummer day of the ox) and consuming {梅干|うめぼ}し (pickled plums) for energy.
